questions.prompt: According to Robert C. Martin, the architecture of a software system is...

options.text: The shape given to the system: its division into components, their arrangement, and how they communicate
The choice of programming language only

questions.explanation: Martin defines architecture as the shape given to the system: the division into components, their arrangement, and how they communicate, to facilitate development, deployment, operation, and maintenance.

questions.prompt: The architecture of a system has very little to do with whether the system works; the value of software behavior differs from the value of software structure.
questions.explanation: The slides state architecture has little to do with whether the system works: value of sw behavior != value of sw structure.

questions.prompt: Which are stated goals of a software architecture?

options.text: Keep the system valuable for its users over time
Minimize the lifetime cost of the system
Maximize the number of lines of code

questions.explanation: Goals: keep the system valuable over time, minimize lifetime cost, and maximize programmer productivity by making it easy to understand, develop, maintain, deploy, and change.

questions.prompt: In the Clean Architecture, what does an 'Entity' contain?

options.text: Critical business rules operating on critical business data

questions.explanation: An Entity contains a set of critical business rules operating on critical business data; it holds the most general high-level rules, rarely changed.

questions.prompt: In the Clean Architecture, which way do source code dependencies point?
questions.explanation: The Dependency Rule states source code dependencies point only inward, toward higher-level policies (inner circles change less than outer mechanisms).

questions.prompt: What does a use case specify in the Clean Architecture?

options.text: Input from users/systems, the output to return, and the processing steps
The exact SQL queries to run

questions.explanation: A use case describes software behavior: the input to be provided, the output to be returned, and the processing steps; it determines the flow of data to and from entities.

questions.prompt: In the separation of policy from details, low-level components (like the Database) know about higher-level components, but not vice versa.
questions.explanation: Low-level components know everything about the higher-level components but not vice versa; the DB component knows about the use-case rules, deferring detail decisions as long as possible.

questions.prompt: Which of these belongs in the outermost 'Frameworks and Drivers' layer?
questions.explanation: Frameworks and drivers (database, web framework, drivers, I/O devices) are details in the outermost layer where you usually write little code.
